lines.english: "She's really going at it…"
"Yeah…"
"All right, let's jump in together on three, Haruki-kun."
"One, two…!"
"Ah! I was supposed to be doing the counting!"
"Congratulations on your graduation!"
"…Make sure to clean this up later."
With a piece of confetti still stuck on her head, Touma was so overwhelmed that she couldn't express her emotions properly.
"Isn't it great, Kazusa? Having your graduation settled before the winter break!"
"Her plans for the future are yet to be determined, though!"
"…I only passed the remedials."
"But your grades are all fine now, right?
From now on, you just have to meet attendance, and your graduation is as good as decided!"
"I don't think it's in the school's interest to keep someone like you around for another year either."
"…Kitahara, how about we settle this outside?"
It's the closing ceremony of the second term.
For third-year students who have potentially life-changing events like university entrance exams and job applications coming up, today is basically the final day when one's graduation is decided.
Today, on this very diverging point of one's life, Touma Kazusa finally managed to earn a passing grade in all of her subjects.
…And while I'm at it, Setsuna and I had already accomplished that without breaking a sweat a week ago.
Now that it's over, those nine remedial exams over five subjects are just pleasant memories we can reminisce about.
…I feel sleepy again today.
"Hey, since our winter break has just officially started without any issues, why don't we all go to karaoke and…"
"No way."
Setsuna already had her fun hogging the mic and enjoying herself a while ago. Neither of us can deal with her when it comes to karaoke.
"I can finally play the piano as much as I want. I think I'll go back to playing over ten hours a day after all this time."
"Ah…"
As always, even during our conversation, Touma's fingers hadn't stopped moving for a second.
"You've started playing the piano again…"
"If there's one good thing about me, it would have to be this."
"You're right about that…"
"Come over here for a second and turn around. I'll give you a nice, hard kick."
Her fingers are moving as lightly as ever, but even the tone of her voice seems to match the mood of her fingers today.
Her words and her expression seem to have brightened up just a little bit as well.
"I'm thinking about entering a competition… for the first time in two years."
"Huh…"
…I stand corrected. Forget the "just a little bit" part.
"…Really? That's wonderful, Kazusa!"
"I'd like to say that everyone can enter, but… that's obviously not the case. At the very least, I can get a recommendation, though."
"Even so, that's amazing… We'll make sure to go cheer you on! Right, Haruki-kun?"
"Ah, yeah!"
Seeing this change in her makes me very happy too.
When I first met her in spring, I saw an extremely irritable classmate. And on that day, I swore that would eventually make her change…
And I'm seeing the change in her that I once imagined right now.
"That's amazing, Touma. We'll make sure to go watch."
"…Don't you dare fall asleep in the concert hall. I'll be keeping my eyes on you."
It's just that…
I feel the slightest sense of defeat after seeing how optimistic she seems to be right now.
"Hey, hold on. If you won this competition, would you be able to get a recommendation to a music university?"
"Winning it right now is pretty much impossible… Besides, you can't get a recommendation for something like that anyway."
"No, no. You just need Touma Youko's influence, see."
"That's right… If Kazusa's mom were to get involved, any music university would accept her, right?"
"And even if that doesn't work, if we use the Touma family's financial assets…"
"…You guys really need to stop making a joke of my family situation. I can't even get angry at you when you're so brazenly talking behind my back."
"Can you really say it's behind your back when we're doing it right in front of you? We're just being a little envious here."
"That's rich, coming from the sheltered son of an affluent family from Okayama."
"Huh, what do you mean? I never heard anything about that!
Haruki-kun, you're leaving me out again!"
"Huh? Wait, no, that's… Touma!"
"Isn't this a textbook example of poetic justice?"
"Well, I did have to make use of my mother's influence a bit, but this competition is really just a gauge of my skill."
"Is that so…"
In both the instant it took for Setsuna to start pouting, and during the several minutes it took to calm her down…
Touma, still not stopping her fingers, just stared and laughed at us.
…She laughed.
"I've been playing on my own without an instructor for the past two years… The competition won't be easy enough for me to win with this kind of effort."
"Even so, this is you we're talking about, Kazusa…"
"I know my own skill the best. Considering the level I'm at now, it would be a miracle if I even made it to the finals. Well, that said, I still wouldn't be losing to those guys in the music class."
"Ah, ahaha…"
"In any case, for now… I want to remember."
"Your skill at your peak?"
"No… in the past, when I was sure I really loved the piano despite who I was."
"In the past…?"
"Who knows… It feels like I forgot all about it while rebelling against my mom…"
Even while uttering such self-deprecating words…
"…How I felt like in the past when I stood in front of the piano."
By now, Touma can no doubt look back to her past in a positive light.
"Or how I was able to spend more than ten hours in front of the piano without complaining even once…?"
Her bitter smile is… not bitter at all. This isn't like the Touma I know.
"…Don't I sound stupid?"
"Not at all… I think this is a great development."
Meaning that the side of herself that Touma had been showing me up until now was the fake one.
"After all, Touma, you've been calling her 'mom' for a while now."
"Ah…"
Meaning that the Touma who referred to her mother as "that person," was never showing me her true self.
"Now that you mention it… you're right."
Which means that the real Touma is someone who's this honestーsomeone who smiles so easily.
"Haha… Even though I hated her so much. Somehow, I guess it's all working out."
This is the Touma I'd never known about.
"That's a good start. There's nothing wrong with getting along with your parents."
"I don't want to hear that from you, Kitahara. You haven't even met your mother face to face more than three times a week this whole year."
"Hey, I told you that's…"
"Wait… What's this all about? 'Hated her so much' and 'haven't met your mother face to face'…"
"Ah, I swear, you're just…"
"Ah?"
As Setsuna threatens to stiffen up again, I pull her toward me and start messing with her sweet-scented hair.
Setsuna protests and pretends that she doesn't like it in response, of course, but she doesn't try to push my hands away.
"Hey, Touma. Before Setsuna gets all pouty again, would you mind if I told her about all that?"
Before she can react, I embrace Setsuna's shoulders and gently stroke her hair.
"I guess there's no other way. Setsuna will cry if you don't, for sure."
Touma accepts my actions with a bitter smile.
"I think she'll cry even if I do tell her. Setsuna gets along really well with her mom, after all. I think she'll be really shocked if she hears about our family situations, you know?"
"S-Stop making fun of me, you two! You're making me sound like an overbearing girl who easily misunderstands everything."
"…Well, part of that might not be far from the truth."
"Yep, I wholeheartedly agree."
Everything is alright. All three of us are heading in a good direction.
Among the three of us, Touma is now able to laugh again. She has become someone who can smile much more brightly than she used to in the past.
Among the three of us, Setsuna and I have naturally deepened our bond.
So everything is alright. There's nothing to worry about.
As long as I can get over it, we'll be able to keep going just like this, with everyone laughing together.
"Good morning, Haruki-kun."
"Hey, good morning."
"You're early as usual. It's still fifteen minutes till the meeting time."
"Well, I'm the type of person who can't settle down unless I'm at the meeting place 30 minutes before schedule…"
"Ahaha… I could say that it's just like you, Haruki-kun, but…"
"But?"
"Well, you know… there are times when I feel like I want to get all nervous and excited waiting for you to show up, Haruki-kun."
"Well, it's just a silly complaint from a girl, so feel free to let it slide."
"Sorry… I couldn't think of a clever comeback."
To begin with, I was just using my usual demeanor as a pretext for the unsightly truth, being the fact that I couldn't get a wink of sleep last night.
"Like I said, just let it slide. If you take it that seriously, I might really get my hopes up."
"Sorry, again and again…"
It's December 24th…
On this very day, the plan that Setsuna imposed on all of us finally begins to unfold.
…In other words, our hot springs trip.
It's been a month since we started dating, and we'll be spending our Christmas at the hot springs.
Not at a restaurant, not at a cafe, not alone together in a room, but at the hot springs.
…And we're staying overnight. Not to mention the fact that it'll be a guy and two girls.
What in the world was everyone doing when they let her get away with this plan that sounds absolutely insane to me? What were they thinking?
Did nobody consider trying to stop her? Like, me, for example?
"Hey, Setsuna."
"Hmm? What is it?"
"I just need to make sure of this againーdid your father really approve of this? I am coming with you, after all."
"Eh…"
"Was it okay for me not to go and explain this at your place this time? You know, like the time we stayed over at Touma's?"
"Why aren't you saying anything?"
"Kazusa sure is late, huh?"
"Why are you changing the subject?"
No, in fact, she's blatantly trying to avoid eye contact with me.
I suppose I can safely say that the suspicion I've been harboring for a while now is slowly turning into certainty.
"Alright, I'm going to ask again. Setsuna, don't tell me…"
"…It's Kazusa."
"Don't try to trick me like that."
Setsuna told a lie, of all things, during the emergency family meeting this time.
"I'm telling you, it really is Kazusa…"
"No one's come out of the station. And I know that the next train doesn't arrive for another five minutes."
On top of that, she even went as far as to try to hide it from me.
"No, that's not what I mean, look behind you…"
"That's where the roundabout is…"
"Sorry for the wait!"
In an attempt to stop Setsuna's excuses, I turn around, expecting to see no one…
"Right, let's load up your luggage and get going.
…Uh, how do I open the trunk again?"
"…Wait a minute, what is this!?"
And my whole world is flipped upside down in an instant.
"Wow, amazing! This is a foreign-made car, isn't it?"
To be more specific, one with a blue and white circular emblem… and a logo with three letters…
Put simply, this is an automobile. A high-class import vehicle, at that. It must cost several million yen, to put it into perspective.
"There were two of these in my garage, so I borrowed one. I also had a maintenance check performed to make sure it works fine today."

Given the direction the car's facing, and the fact that she's sticking her head out from the driver's side window on the front left, it looks like that the car drove through the roundabout in the opposite direction, too…
"Who's going to drive this thing!?"
"I'll be driving, of course. Who do you think drove it all the way here?"
"You have a license!?"
"I got it during summer break. You know that I didn't have anything to do back then."
"Just to make sure, have you driven at all after getting the license…?"
"Of course not. You two were pushing me around for nearly the entire second term, so I had no time to be driving…"
"Um, Kazusa? Is it just me, or is this spot on the front right dented a bit?"
The argument we were having just a moment ago now seems cute, almost too cute compared to this situation…
"Come on, let's hurry up and go. Hey, Kitahara, can you open the trunk?"
"All right then. Let's go, Touma… back to your garage."
"You don't have to worry so much. It's fine if it gets damaged."
"And will you be taking responsibility if people are 'damaged'!?"
"I'm telling you, it'll be fine. I'll drive safely."
"It takes someone who already knows how to drive to be able to drive safely simply by paying attention…"
"Come on, Haruki-kun, hurry up and get in. Let's leave Tokyo before the traffic gets busy!"
"Setsuna…"
Before I knew it, Setsuna had already started poking her head out through the window of the front passenger seat.
I was afraid this would happen… a majority of two votes in favor and one against.
"Hey, Setsuna. Could you get out? Let's take the train after all, yeah?"
"The car's more convenient. We don't have to carry our luggage and we can keep chatting all the way."
I was too focused on the argument itself and overlooked the crucial developments behind the scenes. Swaying the public vote in opposition should have been my priority.
The moment Touma successfully got Setsuna inside the car, my defeat was probably as good as decided.
"But I have a responsibility to your parents to take care of you, Setsuna… If we get into an accident and you get hurt…"
"Certainly, if Setsuna becomes 'damaged goods,' it will be your responsibility, Kitahara."
"Shut up! Ahh, give me a break here… You two don't even realize the gravity of the situation!"
"It's okay. We both know better than anyone that Kazusa can do anything."
"Setsuna…"
That unreasonable belief was my specialty until a month ago.
"There's no way I would put the two of you in danger, right? Just trust me."
"Touma…"
Despite refusing to accept all of this, I realize that it would be impossible to overturn this decision at this point, so I hesitantly get into the back seat.
"Wha… and it's even a manual…"
Driver's seat on the left side, manual transmission stick, and several million yen…
Just bringing a car alone would make for a headache, but this is like a triple handicap straight out of a nightmare.
Please save me, Helen Keller…
"Hey, Kazusa, which one of these buttons is the stereo? I brought some CDs with me…"
"…Is this it?"
I'm supposed to be enjoying this trip, but there's a dark cloud looming over me.
"…The Kanto region will have very cloudy skies during the day, and snowfall is expected during the night, primarily in the mountain range. Up next are the forecasts for each region in the country…"
"That's great. Looks like we'll see some snow."
A dark cloud…
Snow on her first time driving… through the Northern Kanto mountain range?
A quadruple handicap!?
"Off we go, then. Make sure to fasten your seatbelts, everyone."
"Touma… for starters, drive where I tell you to."
"As long as you don't tell me to go home."
"First, let's buy a map from a bookstore, then let's go to an auto parts store to buy winter emergency supplies. Chains, antifreeze, jump cables… do we have any of those?"
In that case, it's my duty to protect the two in the front seats with my life.
"I'm amazed you knew I haven't prepared any of those."
"Haruki-kun really leaves nothing to chance, huh?"
"Haah…"
I don't actually feel good at all about having to put my life on the line for a mere domestic trip.
"Okay then, let's go…"
"Half clutch is… kinda difficult."
"No, you've got the handbrake on…"
"Ah, right, that's right. Since this car has left and right flipped, I keep forgetting."
"Sorry, change of plans. Let's go to a pharmacy first."
"Haruki-kun, are you getting motion sickness?"
"No… I need some stomach medicine."
And it's hurting pretty bad already.
And just like that…
"Kazusa, are you okay?"
"Don't talk to me… If I lose focus even for a moment, it'll be dangerous."
"S-Sorry."
"Ah, Touma, turn left at that light…"
"I told you not to talk to me!"
"…But how am I supposed to…"
At long last…
"Ah, there's the highway tollgate!"
"O-Okay… Now, just need to switch to the left lane…"
"No, don't enter. It's absolutely impossible for you to drive on the highway in your current condition."
"A-Alright."
"But, you know, my dad told me that it's actually much easier for new drivers to drive on highways."
"R-Really…?"
"You're definitely incapable of merging into traffic right now. Let's just take local roads until you're a little more used to driving."
"A… little more…?"
"Well, taking local roads is fine for now since they run parallel to the highway, but it looks like they'll separate after the next interchange."
"Here, give me the map… Ah, you're right. What now?"
"I'm sure it'll work out. As long as we keep driving on the outermost lane."
"Hm… Fair enough. Let's call it a learning experience. Touma, let's take the highway after all…"
"We just passed the entrance!"
After numerous twists and turns…
"…I knew it, Kazusa can do anything!"
"It's a piece of cake once you get used to it. Cars and musical instruments are both tools in essence."
"Nevertheless, don't lose your focus. A small lapse in focus can be enough to prove fatal."
"You do nothing but preach from dawn till dusk, Kitahara. You sure have a big mouth for someone who can't even drive himself."
"Accidents are most likely to occur when you start thinking that you've gotten used to something. You can nag all you want after you've made it to the inn and turned off the engine."
"Come on, I can freely change lanes and pass other cars now."
"Wow… So fast!"
"…Hold on, you're going over 1X0 km/h!"
After numerous twists and turns… Wait, I just said that.
"Umm, uhhh…"
"…Where are we?"
"Haruki-kun…"
"Losing your way… That's the most fatal mistake a navigator can make, Kitahara."
"That's why I've been apologizing for a good while now!"
"I don't seem to remember you apologizing even once…"
"That's because I believe the best way to apologize right now is to get us back on the right path…"
"Good to know you're still peerless when it comes to making excuses."
"Hey, maybe we should have turned right at that fork in the road earlier?"
"Ah! The sun is setting!?"
…Our journey is about to come to an end.
…No, we're still in the middle of our journey.
"There's no doubt about it… we're finally gonna hit the jackpot this time."
"We saw the Hakuga Hot Springs Station earlier, right? So if we just follow the map on the pamphlet from here… Aaah, what a relief!"
"All that's left is a straight road ahead. At least Kitahara won't be able to lead me astray anymore."
"Good to know you're still peerless when it comes to fault-finding."
"I merely adjust my responses based on who I'm talking to."
…Regardless of the antagonistic conversation, both Touma and I, as well as Setsuna, were finally able to relax a little.
…That disaster from an hour ago was pretty bad. We'd been talking less and less after that.
"It's a good thing that the weather didn't give us any trouble. Seems like it held out for us until the end."
"We did buy chains and all that other stuff, so it's kind of a waste."
"Ah…"
We even bought a flashlight at the auto parts store because the salesperson recommended it, bringing the total cost to over three people's worth of roundtrip train tickets.
"By failing to prepare, you are preparing to fail. I say some pretty cool things sometimes, huh?"
"Is that your own proverb…? I swear, you're always so full of it…"
"Guys, look!"
"Eh?"
"Ah…"
Setsuna pointed through the windshield…
And suddenly, numerous large snowflakes started fluttering down outside.
In no time at all, they dyed the outside world from black to white.
"It's started falling…"
"Well, that's that. It is coming down at the end, after all."
"Let's go see the snow!"
Our little adventure started with that one suggestion made by Setsuna.
Passing through the valleys and across the hills, we lost our way and drove back and forth over and over.
We're already way past our planned arrival time, and it's completely dark outside.
"So white…"
"Looks like it'll pile up tonight."
"Yeah…"
But it's thanks to all that time we lost trying to find our way that we are able to experience this moment.
"It's… beautiful."
That's why we feel grateful for the chain of coincidences we're experiencing right now… Grateful to no one in particular, yet also to everyone.
"What the…?"
"Ahh!?"
Uh-oh…?
"Wow…"
"Oops…"
"How in the…"
Setsuna looks up to the sky, while Touma and I stare at the car.
And then, each of us lets out a sigh of astonishment for our own reasons.
"What is this…? How did it build up this much already?"
Before we even realized it, the snow had set in across the road we were driving on, and we were surrounded by walls of snow on both sides.
Touma's car then skidded on the snow-paved road and collided into the white wall, with the left-side doors completely buried in it.
"There wasn't a trace of snow up until now."
Making our way into the mountain roads and distracted by the snow falling from the sky, we received a baptism by the snow that hadn't melted from before.
"Snow… There's snow all around us! We're finally here!"
"No, our destination is still a bit further…"
The distraction that the falling snow provided coupled with the trap created by the piled-up snow on the ground completely screwed us over.
"Haha, aha… Ahahaha! You were right, Kitahara… A small lapse in focus proved to be fatal."
"A winch! The road service! No, I'll run to the inn first…"
"Take this!"
"Bwuahh!?"
As I was losing my mind over how careless I'd been, divine punishment struck me like a bolt out of the blue.
"It's cold, it's so cold! We can have a snowball fight! We can build a snowman, too!"
…Guided by the hands of Setsuna, who's become like a small puppy zooming around a garden.
"Ahahahaha, I messed up. I messed up big time. I guess I still have a ways to go."
"Setsuna, not yet, don't start enjoying yourself yet! We have to get the car out of the snow first! And you, Touma, stop laughing and help me over here!"
"Just a little more… After we've made a snowman, okay?"
"Wow, it's really coming down. It'd be funny if we got buried under the snow together with the car at this rate. Hehe, ahaha…"
"…Come ooon…"
It's hopeless. They've both lost it.
It's been a fairly surreal day, riddled with surreal events.

After making countless mistakes from dawn till dusk and getting ourselves in trouble over and over again, we've come to find our misfortunes amusing, and we've started laughing and enjoying ourselves.
"What can you do, huh…?"
A day as unique as this has its own charm, no doubt.
With this thought in mind, and seeing the two in front of me enjoying themselves and laughing sincerely…
I find myself overwhelmed with joy as well.
"Just as the white snow softly fills the city's streets…♪"
"We're deep in the mountains, though."
"Okay, then… Merry Christmas!"
"M-Merry Christmas."
"Merry… Christmas…"
With two oolong teas and some artificially flavored orange juice, we make a proper toast.
…Never mind the issue of whether there's anything proper about having one male student and two female students on an overnight trip at a mountain hot springs.
"Wow, it looks delicious…
Celebrating Christmas with sashimi, tempura, and hot pot isn't half bad either, right?"
"Christmas pudding and steamed egg custard are kind of similar… ingredient-wise."
"We also have chicken… floating like dumplings inside the pot."
After all that happened, we somehow managed to contact the inn staff and were promptly rescued.
"But wow, it's really amazing outside. It's a white Christmas."
"Yeah, really."
"That's exactly why we picked this place, after all."
After telling us that accidents happen a lot on this road, the inn employee used his four-wheel drive vehicle to expertly tow our car out of the snow.
"By the way, the open air hot springs were amazing! There's no roof, so the snow falls right inside the bath."
"It was so cold… I thought I was going to freeze to death as I came out of the water."
"It's true that it was cold, but it felt really good. You should have gone and tried it out too, Haruki-kun."
"I didn't have any energy left for that…"
As soon as we arrived at the inn, I was rapidly overcome with fatigue from the day and passed out on the room's floor until dinnertime.
"For spending so much energy, you weren't all that helpful."
"You guys sure are full of energy…"

Meanwhile, Touma, who drove for hours, and Setsuna, who was hyper for hours, have been enjoying everything one can on a hot springs trip. Ever since we arrived, they've been exploring the inn, searching for souvenirs to buy, taking a bath, and playing ping pong.
"Must be because we've been training differently until now. Especially during the past two months, I hardly had time to sleep."
"November was my fault, sure, but you brought December upon yourself…"
Besides, I went through the same thing as her.
"Looking back, it's been a really difficult year. Okay, drink up, let's drink!"
"Setsuna, you're making this feel like a year-end party."
"This clearly is a year-end party. If you claimed this was a Christmas party, westerners would scorn you."
Choosing this place for our trip may have been where we went all wrong, for starters…
"It doesn't matter whether this is a Christmas party or a year-end party. I'm here with the people I want to be with."
"Okay, okay, Princess Setsuna. Your wish is our command."
In any case, if I rationally look at myself sharing a hot pot with two beautiful girls who just came out of their baths in sexy yukatas…
"Well, why not. Merry Christmas!"
Honestly, I'm so happy I could die here right now.
I hate how the atmosphere is definitely making me sound like an old man here, but no matter how I look at it, this situation is already criminal.
"Ahem. I'd like to say thank you to everyone for taking time out of your busy lives to join us here today."
…Though I already know that moments as enjoyable as these are sure to pass by in a flash.
The feast that had been laid out on the table is already finished, and it's time for everyone to close out the year-end party with a toast.
"We're gathered here today for a Christmas party, a year-end party, a graduation trip that's a little early… and, umm…"
"Ah, that's right. You could also call this a reunion party for the Houjou High School Light Music Club!"
"A reunion…? It's not like we're disbanding, though, are we?"
Sorry… Takeya. I'll never forget about you.
…Of course, I'm not so stupid as to bring your name up here. You of all people should understand, right?
"Then, let's call it the Light Music Club group reunion number 0… How's that?"
I mean, just look at how happy our host is today.
"This is number 0, okay? We'll do number 1 and number 2… We'll have as many as you'd like, okay?"
"What I mean is, I want us to meet up again next year on this day. Watching the snow, taking baths together, chatting into the night…"
If there's anything that could ruin her smile…
"…I can't promise that, Setsuna."
"Eh…"
I couldn't possibly do it, but…
There was no way for me to stop Touma from uttering that either.
"I have no idea what will happen in the future. I'm on a different path from you two. The same day, next year… I can't promise that."
"B-But… no matter how busy you get, just once a year should…"
"But hey, what if I got a boyfriend?"
…I've made a mistake.
The first person to be taken aback by that proclamation should have been Setsuna.
"And then, if I end up only thinking about that person constantly, every single day, and start to not care about my old friends anymore…"
"Come on, stop that… Why are you bringing that up right now…? It's Christmas, isn't it?"
The reason I'm stopping Touma right now is supposed to be in consideration of Setsuna's feelings.
"Exactly because it's Christmas, okay? Isn't this a day one would normally spend with their lover?"
"That only applies to Japan. In other countries, it's a day to spend time with your family or go to church, you know."
I wasn't supposed to stop Touma simply because I… didn't want to hear her talk about that.
"Same goes for you, Setsuna. You might change your mind and want to be alone with Kitahara next year. If that happens, the promise we make here today could prove to be a hindrance."
"Whenever the three of us are together, it has to be all three of us, always…"
"Setsuna…"
"It can't be the two of us, or just one of us. It has to be the three of us."
The warm and pleasant mood is slowly freezing over now, just like the feeling of emerging from an open-air bath in the hot springs while it's snowing.
"Whenever the three of us are together, Haruki-kun is a precious friend of mine. And whenever the three of us are together, Kazusa is a friend I wouldn't trade for anything."
"…Can't it work like that?"
That is exactly the way Setsuna is acting right now.
Whenever the three of us are together, she tries her best not to act like my girlfriend.
At first, and because it was so early in our relationship, she couldn't control herself at times. But around the time our finals started, she began to draw a clear line.
Rather than merely following our three-second rule, Setsuna has been holding back from doing anything that might involve that rule recently.
"…Are you suggesting that you want me, and even Kitahara, to keep playing house like this with you every year?"
"Touma, stop it…"
Even so, Touma continues to provoke us, threatening to cross a line that shouldn't be crossed.

"That's just… terribly convenient for you. Utterly selfish and self-centered. You're completely disregarding your friend's and your boyfriend's personal thoughts on the matter. Can't you see how unbelievably egoistic that is?"
I don't know what lies beyond that line. There may not even be anything there. Though I admit that I feel an instinctive urge to peer into that abyss.
To catch a glimpse of Touma's true feelings.
"It's true that it's selfish. It is a dream… that I've envisioned all by myself."
Despite being confronted with such a dark sentiment, Setsuna firmly stares back at Touma with resolve in her eyes.
"But I can't help it… After all, the three of us stood together on that stage, didn't we?"
"Ah…"
That's no different from my own thoughts at all. It feels like something that I would say.

"The three of us sang, played and worked on the song for an entire night. The three of us waited in excitement for the curtain to rise. The three of us… were cheered by the audience together, were we not?"
…In fact, I once confronted Touma with words that were meant to convey the exact same meaning, just like how Setsuna is now.
"I want to talk about that day forever. I want to remember it for years to come. And if possible… I want to sing with you two backing me once again."
Ah, that's right… I remember.
It was the day that I revealed to Touma that I was dating Setsuna.
"…Sorry. Thinking about what I just said, it really is terribly selfish."
Setsuna's just like me.
She holds no reservations toward the two others present with her, and confidently expresses her love toward them.
And that's precisely why I feel unsure sometimes.
On that night… why did Setsuna urge me into making a decision?
"…If you're going to go that far, let me see you prove it."
In response to Setsuna's stare and feelings, Touma replies after a short silence, and glares back.
"W-What do you mean?"
She slowly reaches behind her back…
And then puts her hand on the table once again.
"To eternal friendship."
With her thumb already on the cork of the bottle.
"That's… How am I supposed to…
Kya!?"
"Whoa!?"
A high-pitched pop echoes throughout the room.
"If you really want the three of us to stay together, Setsuna, I'll have you accompany me to the bitter end today."
"Huh?"
Then, the sizzling sound of the carbonated drink softly fills the room.
"We're drinking till morning. I am absolutely not letting you sleep."
The bottle's label reads "Champagne," and underneath that label is a brand name that I feel like I've seen somewhere before.
"Eh? Eh?"
"Vintage" is written further below, along with four numbers that most likely represent the year it was made.
Wait, isn't this one of those famous brands only people at high-class Ginza bars drink…?
"Once again, Merry Christmas! Ahahaha, come on, Setsuna, you're taking this way too seriously!"
"Eeeehh!?"
"Heey, Setsuna. How about another glass?"
"Ah… Uwaahhh… She totally played me… Kazusa just totally made me embarrass myself!"
"Ahahaha… Setsuna, you're so adorable. If I were a guy, I would never let someone like Kitahara have you."
"Keep me out of this."
"I'd never let a cruel guy like Kazusa deceive me! Gulp, gulp… Hwaa…!"
…Even while complaining like this, Setsuna snuggles up against Kazusa.
Probably too embarrassed from being played on, she drank each of the three glasses Touma poured in a single go.
Of course, only after doing so did she appear to realize that what she was drinking wasn't one of those 200-yen carbonated drinks you enjoy with your family at Christmas parties.
"A cruel guy, huh…? That's right, I wouldn't be her type. Her boyfriend is the complete opposite of me… Make her happy, Kitahara."
"Bwuh!?"
I was naive to think Setsuna was the only one drunk.
"Heey, don't talk about steamy stuff like that now! All right? Whenever the three of us are together～"
"Yes, yes. It has to be all three of us, always. I didn't forget, Setsuna. There, there."
"Yes, thass right! It's always three! Haruki-kun is here, Kazusa is here, and eye'm… Wahahaha…!"
"Wait, hey, Setsuna… don't cling to me like that… H-Hey, Kitahara…"
"Don't cry to me for help. You're the one who made her drink. You reap what you sow."
Actually, it's more like I find this scene of two girls clinging to each other while only wearing their thin yukatas to be way too sexy.
I refuse to break up such a wonderful scene. I swear upon my life to preserve this in its natural state.
"Mmmm… Kazusa, your hair is so silky. I saw you in the bath too, your skin was all whiite…"
"I'd say your skin is whiter, Setsuna… and your back is so smooth too."
"Ehehe… Thanks. Aaah, it smells so good…"
"Ah, wait… Setsuna?"
"Mm… mmm…"
"…Aa-ah…"
"Good work there. Want another glass?"
"I don't think I can stand not drinking at this point."
"A textbook example of poetic justice indeed."
Touma swiftly downs another glass after allowing the exhausted Setsuna, who was already leaning against her, to lie on her lap.
And I turn my head away as if to say, "this has nothing to do with me."

…But even though I've turned my head away, I keep catching glimpses of the curves sticking out around their chests, their legs stretching out bewitchingly from the hems of their clothing, and other fantastic regions.
…I'm glad that we came here. But if I could make a single wish, I'd like just a little time for myself. Like, right now.
"Anyway… Kitahara, you seem pretty sober."
"Well… this stuff is delicious."
"Is that the actual reason?"
"A long time ago, I went to one of Takeya's gatherings and tried some cheap 390-yen per bottle wine, but I felt like vomiting after the third glass."
Naturally, I'll skip the part about the occasion having been a cosplay porn viewing event.
"Well, maybe you've got a little fat in your stomach now?"
"That makes it sound like there's something wrong with my metabolism."
"This stuff is probably several tens of thousands of yen per bottle. My mom sent it from France."
"Bourgeois as ever, aren't we…?"
"I normally drink cheap port wine. This is ridiculously sweet and delicious in comparison."
"No, just don't drink normally to begin with."
"Come on, I'm a delinquent, you know? I've gotta act at least a bit like one, or I'll be setting a bad example, you know?"
"What's a really bad example is how you're old-fashionably labeled a delinquent in this day and age."
When even stereotypes like delinquents and trendy gyarus are becoming obsolete these days, who'd imagine there's still someone going against the adults head on…
"That's right… Over the past two years, I've been going around and acting like an old-fashioned idiot."
"I'm sure you'll die of embarrassment once you grow up and tell people about your past."
When that time comes, I'll be the one telling the story to everyone… I wouldn't mind seeing an adult Touma blushing and seething with rage.
"Yet what am I doing now? Hanging out with prim and proper people like the class president and a school idol, seriously participating in a school festival, studying, having fun…"
"Pretending that just drinking and messing around like this is some kind of huge event…"
"…Heh, you evolved."
"You'd call this evolution?"
"At the very least, you've become more like a modern person."
"A modern person, huh?"
"Whether you would call it a profession or art, you're playing music to stand out, and you've dropped the lame act of pretending to be aloof and isolated."
"…That's not very convincing coming from someone who's been acting like an honors student, which is even more lame and old-fashioned."
"That's why I tried to cut loose a little. Like breaking school rules, taking up music to look cool… and going on a trip with girls."
"…That last one is super modern person-like. I'm amazed a guy like you could pull it off, Kitahara."
"Even though it's a trip to hot springs in the mountains."
"The snow isn't letting up, huh?"
"You're right."
"It's pure white."
"Will we be able to leave tomorrow?"
"…You're right."
Until now, I would have asked a tasteless question like that.
But I've begun to understand just a little what it's like to be romantic, as well as what would be considered tasteless.
"…What?"
"Nothing…"
That's why I don't turn my gaze away even when Touma realizes I'm quietly staring at her.
"…Really."
And… There, Touma turned her eyes away first. I win.
Her face is slightly blushed.
Because of that, it's impossible for me to turn my eyes away.
"It's pretty."
"Y-Yeah… It's all white."
"Right… White and smooth, wasn't it?"
"T-That's… Setsuna."
"I see…"
"Mm… mm…"
"Ahh…"
I blanked out for an hour trying to sober myself up.
Then, I enjoyed the sight of Setsuna sleeping on Touma's lap and Touma dozing off while leaning against the wall for a little while before quietly leaving the room.
Of course, I didn't forget to cover those two with blankets.
Because it's late at night, and since there are hardly any guests staying overnight, I pretty much have the entire bath area to myself.
…Is this inn going to be okay, financially? It'd be a waste of such great hot springs.
"Aaahh…"
As I settle into the vacant bath, my voice spills out in amazement, fading into the night sky together with the fluttering white snowflakes.
The snow that began at nightfall shows no signs of letting up, and it cools down the hot water a little as it falls into the bath.
I take a moment to look at the white snow falling from the sky, then slowly close my eyes, and relax my entire body.
But as I willingly submit myself to darkness, the most recent scenery I saw immediately comes to mind.
"…Calm down."
The sight of the two girls sleeping so nonchalantly near me while leaning against each other, as if they had been close friends for years.

I thank whichever deity made it possible for me to bear witness to that momentーI suppose I should pray to God given that it's Christmasー and I finally came to a conclusion as I continue staring at the sight that I can't get enough of.
Every time I meet with Setsuna, every time I touch her, it's like she always manages to thrust an adorable new side of herself onto me…
And Touma… she's even more beautiful now than ever before.
I misjudged her.
Ever since I met her, regardless of her personality and attitude, I always believed that her sublimely crafted beauty would never change.
I believed that it was an impossible miracle given to Touma by chance, and completely separate from her nature.
But I was wrong…
Whenever Touma laughs, teases me, sighs, or looks at me with an expression I can't understand…
Whenever she turns her eyes away from me with an expression I can't understand…
She spectacularly shows off her newfound beauty to me, as if to challenge all of my existing concepts of what beauty is.
Setsuna herself looks incredibly beautiful as she sleeps right next to her, and given she also has a cute side that only I know about, she's so dear to me that I want to embrace her forever.
Even so, my other friend right in front of me… the friend of my girlfriend…
She's the one I'm still longing for from the bottom of my heart.
I'm…
I don't even need to think about it. I'm the worst there is.
As if being chased away, I get up from the bath.
It feels like more and more of my hideousness might leak out if I stay submerged in this hot spring any longer.
For the time being, I'll go back into the room, cover myself with a blanket from head to toe and hopefully sleep through the night dreamlessly.
I'll be sleeping in a corner of the room right next to the girls' room divided by a sliding door, of course.
Who else would want to take a bath at this time of the night…?
"W-Wait… Are you serious? Are you in your right mind, Setsuna? You're still drunk, aren't you!?"
"Hehehe… Am I drunk? Ah, or maybe I'm just sleepwalking, huh?"
"…Huh?"
From the changing room, someone is… no, some people are approaching…
Their silhouettes that were initially hidden by the steam are becoming clearer with every step they take.
"S-Stop… Don't push me! We can't come in here now, he's still…!"
"Ah, there he is. Haruki-kuun!"
"Wha… Aaaaagh!?"
"Aah, hot! Too hot!"
The snow cooled off my body as I came out of the bath, and as I suddenly re-entered, it naturally feels unbearably hot.
Even though it's common sense, it doesn't even occur to me because of the situation I'm in.
"D-Don't look! Don't look at me…"
"That's what I should be saying!"
"You don't get to say stuff like that when we're the ones barging in, Kazusa…"
In front of my eyes, two bath towels… wait, no, that's not what I mean.
I got excited just from seeing their white legs earlier, but this time they're even showing off their dazzling thighs… wait, no!
"W-Why, why exactly…"
With only those towels for cover, their body lines are so visible that it's enough to put me in a bind.
"The bath here is connected on the inside. I realized it earlier when I came in."
"I'm not asking about the method, I'm asking about the motive!"
"I'd like to know as well…"
"Come on, we promised together earlier. Whenever the three of us are together…"
"It has to be all three of us."
"Wait, you meant… even in situations like this!?"
"Uwaah… Large baths feel so nice, huh?"
Setsuna's voice, interspersed with long sighs, echoes together with the sound of her scooping up the water with her hands.
…From right behind me.
"I'm disappointed in you, Touma. You were with her, so how could you allow this blunder to…"
"She's your girlfriend, Kitahara! You do something about it."
"And you're her best friend… Why didn't you stop her?"
We're soaking ourselves in the bath together with almost zero distance between us; we're so close that I can feel the ripples from the water every time Setsuna moves.
"I did try to stop her! I refused! But…"
"Aah, jeez, would you two stop fighting already? It feels so good, so let's all be a bit nicer to each other, okay?"
"How are you so okay with this, Setsuna…?"
Not to mention, Setsuna's shoulders keep brushing against mine. They really are smooth, just like Touma said earlier.
"Because I knew you wouldn't shamelessly stare at us, Haruki-kun. I was sure you would keep your gaze turned away no matter what."
She saw right through me.
"I kept teasing her earlier, remember? …I imagine she was holding a grudge over that."
"Sure, you deserve your payback, that makes sense. But what about me? The two of you are just bullying me here!"
"You're bathing with two girls… What more could you ask for?"
"There should be a limit to things that one can ask for…"
Anyway, in my best attempts to avoid a cliche, I focus on blocking my nostrils to prevent any bleeding.
"It's fine, isn't it? People say to forget any sense of shame when you go on a trip, right? Even if it's embarrassing now, it'll make for a good memory someday!"
"…I feel like Touma will hit me every time I try to remember it."
"What a coincidence, Kitahara. I was actually just imagining the same situation. Clenching my fist and swinging it full force."
"These are such nice hot springs, with such great scenery, right? Let's enjoy ourselves more."
"It's pitch black, though."
"Can't see anything but the snow, though."
"No matter how many times I look, I won't get tired of this sight…"
Completely ignoring our banter, Setsuna happily looks up at the snowy sky.
Given how astonished and cheerful she is, as well as how much she's relishing the situation, one could assume that this is her first time seeing snow.
"Aa-ah… This is the best. I don't want to go back."
"Setsuna…"
While looking up at the sky, Setsuna rests her head on my shoulder.
I can smell the scent of shampoo coming from her wet hair. And I can feel the pleasant weight of someone leaning against me with the slightest hint of restraint.
"I feel kind of sleepy… If I fall asleep, please carry me to the room, okay?"
"M-Me?"
If I were to stick to proper bathing etiquette, that would mean carrying Setsuna with only a towel on?
"That's fine. It would be an accident if it happened, so I can't blame you for sneaking a peek."
"Eh, um…"
"Just no match for Setsuna, huh…"
"You're one to talk, after making me cry a river earlier there, Kazusa."
"I was barely making a small quip there, while you're unleashing this overkill retaliation on me for it."
While saying that…
I'm sure that Touma, too, is gracefully relaxing her entire body as she gazes absentmindedly at the snowy sky.
"There's no way a nobody like me would ever be a match for Setsuna."
I'm sure, because… I can feel her long, black hair brushing against my shoulders as well.
"I just… can't win…"
And then…
"Touma…?"
"What is it?"
"No, I…"
Our backs are touching… She's definitely aware of it.
Right after Setsuna leaned against me as well, almost as if she were calculating the timing… Although it could just be me overthinking.
"I want to stay like this forever."
"…Yeah."
It seems like the snow is starting to let up a little.
"What's the matter? Are you tired?"
After we got off the highway, Touma stopped the car on the side of the road.
"…Go ahead and join her there."
"Mm… mmm…"
Touma whispers this to me while looking at the back seat through the rear view mirror.
Setsuna has dozed off in the back, and the way her head is tilted makes it look like she could tip over at any moment.
"We're less than an hour away, aren't we? Let's keep going."
"Don't hold back. I don't need a navigator anymore. I know the way from here on."
Setsuna was eagerly talking to us, trying her best to encourage everyone not to fall asleep until a moment ago.
However, maybe because she's relieved that we are getting close to home, she's finally reached her limit.
"I'll pass. I feel like I would also fall asleep immediately if I did that."
"I don't mind if you sleep next to Setsuna. I'll wake you up once we arrive."
However, it's clearly our fault that Setsuna fell asleep.
"It wouldn't be funny if I found myself in heaven when I opened my eyes."
"…You still don't trust my driving skills? I can already go in reverse, make tight turns, parallel park, and all that…"
"I do believe in your skills, but I don't believe that you're not tired."
"I'm telling you, it's fine. I wouldn't fall asleep while driving."
"Even so, the possibility of you falling asleep isn't zero. But if another person is awake next to you, it's a lot closer to zero, right?"
The thing is, we…
We weren't able to fully enjoy the trip until the very end.
"…Suit yourself."
"Yeah, don't mind if I do."
"In that case, if you're going to stay there in the passenger seat, promise me…"
"What?"
"That you absolutely won't fall asleep. I'm afraid I might make a mistake…"
"…Heh, you're not that familiar with the roads here after all. Don't worry, I'll stay awake until we arrive for sure."
"…I'm really counting on you."
We left the inn after having breakfast.
We stopped by a rest stop to have lunch in the middle of our journey, and right around then, the only thing left to do was to head back home.
Touma and I have both been talking noticeably less since.
"Mm…"
In the end…
Our mistake was having too much fun, being too happy.
The end of any festivity is always the hardest part. This time though, it bore down far more heavily than when the school festival ended.
…No, that's not it.
It's because the events after the school festival are still weighing on our minds.
It may be that we're at a loss for words now because our feelings overlap with our feelings from that day, when everything ended and so many things were settled.
"Hey, Kitahara."
"Mm?"
As I was possessed by my lonely thoughts, Touma finally spoke up when we stopped at a red light.
In truth, she'd been trying to speak up for a while now.
However, she would hesitate, and after shaking her head and sighing each time, she'd focus on driving for a little while. Rinse and repeat.
"Thanks for… everything."
"Don't talk like you're leaving behind a will."
After this one phrase from her, I understand the reason behind her recurrent hesitation.
She was trying to do something she is incredibly unused to: thanking me.
"Just let me express my gratitude every once in a while, you imp."
"I haven't really done anything worthy of your gratitude."
Neither of us had the energy to deal with me saying, "I don't want to be called that by you," and start an unnecessary argument over it.
"If you hadn't dragged me out, I would never have turned out like this."
"…Something about the way you're saying that sounds resentful."
"…It does? Sorry, I'll rephrase it a bit."
Even so, Touma goes on in trying to sincerely express her gratitude to me, no matter how humiliating it might feel to her.
"If you and Setsuna had never appeared in my life… I would have spent every day sleeping, doing whatever I wanted, and I would have continued living freely."
"…You're doing this on purpose, aren't you?"
I don't know what exactly spurred her to do that, but at the very least, I can detect an unimaginably resentful air from her attempt to do so.
"N-No… I can't put it into words. I know what I want to say, but it's like my mouth won't cooperate, you know…"
"Ah, that's enough. Receiving gratitude from you is just unpleasant."
"You're awful…"
Nonetheless, it seems like she's really hurt by my words, and that's making me seem awful as a result.
"Not to mention… I was never really expecting any gratitude in return anyway."
"Kitahara…"
That's why I've decided to refuse Touma's words of thanks.
"Everything I've done, I've done because I wanted to, and for my own sake."
I hope Touma can accept this as a reward for her efforts.
"Not even for a moment did I think I was doing anything for you, Touma."
"Setsuna refused the same way when I tried to thank her. Just accept it, would you? It's not fair."
"No way. I'll accept it over my dead body."
Personally, it just feels strange to hear words of gratitude when I don't feel like I've done anything to warrant it.
"You… Is it the same when you stick your nose in other people's business? Do you joyfully do all of that as well?"
"I only do it for you and Setsuna, Touma."
Which is why if I hear any gratitude from anyone else…
I'll make sure to act all cocky, encourage them to reflect on their actions in a simple and detailed manner, and accept their gratitude, as that's the natural thing to do.
And that's because… they're not special to me.
"I'll never… forget those words."
Whereas this particular person who I consider special to me mutters something to herself at the end and starts driving again.
